models_used.note: Vendor-provenance behavioural port. Its own header states it 'does not claim a timing, noise, or temperature model' -- propagation delay is NOT measurable with this model.

v_bus_line_node_identity.resolution_note: CORRECTED 2026-07-27: the 2026-07-26 'resolution' claiming this divider senses the FULL bus was itself wrong -- see docs/STRATEGY.md 'OVP-01 senses the half-bus and is now fail-open'. Proof independent of any comment: PowerInput's c_bus1 is sized against v_bus_half (170V), not the 340V full bus (modules.ato: `assert c_bus1.voltage_rating >= v_bus_half * 1.25`). The spec windows applied by this harness are therefore the HALVED windows (195-205V trip / 5-10V hysteresis), not the full-bus 390-410V/10-20V ones.

verdict.propagation_delay_reason: TLV3201_ngspice.lib declares no timing model; a measured delay from this model would be a modelling artifact, not physical.
verdict.summary: Simulated OVP-01 trip point at the v_bus.line node (dc_bus_plus, the +170V half-bus) is 200.03 V and release point is 191.24 V (uncalibrated), giving 8.79 V of hysteresis. This is WITHIN the half-bus-equivalent 195-205V trip / 5-10V hysteresis requirement (FUNCTIONAL_TEST_CRITERIA.md SS2.2's 390-410V/10-20V full-bus windows, halved), matching the OVPComparator module's own inline hand-derivation (199.95V trip, 191.21V release) to within 0.08 V / 0.03 V. This simulation uses nominal component values only, per METHODOLOGY.md; unlike the prior divider-referenced design (docs/evidence/2026-07-27-ovp01-half-bus-retune.md, 193.9-206.2V worst-case-tolerance-only, failing the 195-205V window before tempco was even added), this REF2025-referenced design (Option C, docs/evidence/2026-07-27-ovp01-ref2025-implementation.md) clears the 195-205V/5-10V windows even at the worst-case tolerance+tempco corner (196.11-203.81V trip, 8.58-8.90V hysteresis at DT=60C) -- that bound comes from a separate hand/script E96 corner analysis, not a SPICE sweep.
